goals: Mechanistic: characterize how peak SWE varies across the Wenatchee elevation gradient
Validation: quantify ELM skill against SNOTEL SWE (magnitude and melt-out timing)
key_processes: snow accumulation (rain/snow partitioning at the freezing level)

model_choice.rationale: Single-column ELM resolves snowpack mass/energy balance per point; the elevation gradient is sampled as a set of columns. Validation is pinned to SNOTEL.

answerable: ELM snow physics skill at SNOTEL points IF elevation-appropriate forcing is supplied
Relative sensitivity of peak SWE to soil/surface properties (secondary, small)

not_answerable.aspect: How peak SWE varies across the elevation gradient
not_answerable.why: Elevation controls peak SWE through air-temperature lapse and orographic precipitation; with uniform gridded forcing across all columns, elevation-stratified columns differ only by soil/surface and will not reproduce the true SWE-elevation relationship.
not_answerable.needs: elevation-downscaled meteorological forcing (T lapse rate + precipitation-elevation adjustment)

not_answerable.aspect: Co-located validation of melt-out timing across the full gradient
not_answerable.why: Only 5 SNOTEL SWE stations exist; dense snow courses are missing, so mid-band and high-alpine SWE cannot be independently validated.
not_answerable.needs: additional in-domain SWE observations (snow course / gridded SWE reanalysis ingest)

sampling_strategy.approach: stratified by elevation band + validation columns pinned to observations
sampling_strategy.n_justification: 5 elevation bands spanning 187-2870 m, with double sampling (2 per band) in and around the rain-snow transition where peak SWE is most sensitive to the freezing level; a single representative column suffices in the low valley and high alpine where the response is near-monotonic. This resolves the gradient shape with minimal columns. NOTE: this design only becomes scientifically valid once elevation-downscaled forcing exists (see feasibility); until then it isolates soil/surface effects, not elevation.
sampling_strategy.placement_logic: Concentrate columns in the 1000-1800 m rain-snow transition band, where a small elevation change flips precipitation phase and drives the steepest peak-SWE gradient; sparser sampling at the low and high extremes.
sampling_strategy.replication: 2 columns per transition band to capture within-band variance where sensitivity is highest; 1 elsewhere.

sampling_plan.reason: Anchors the low-elevation, largely rain-dominated end of the gradient where peak SWE is minimal.
Oversampled because peak SWE is most sensitive here: small elevation changes shift precipitation phase and melt timing.
Oversampled to resolve the steep rise in peak SWE across the freezing-level band.
Core snow-dominated band; sampled to define the peak-SWE maximum and its persistence.
Captures the high-elevation SWE plateau/upper limit and cold-season accumulation.

validation_design.comparison: co-located — validation columns pinned to the 5 SNOTEL station coordinates/elevations, compared per water-year
validation_design.metric: bias and RMSE of peak SWE; date-offset of peak/melt-out

validation_design.comparison: co-located — daily/monthly SWE time series at station points

experiment_summary.primary_treatment: baseline forcing (1980-2018 climatology), native soil; snow spin-up applied

requires_capabilities.capability: elevation-downscaled meteorological forcing (temperature lapse rate + precipitation-elevation adjustment)
requires_capabilities.why: Peak SWE is governed by elevation-dependent temperature (rain/snow phase) and orographic precipitation; uniform forcing cannot reproduce the SWE-elevation gradient.
requires_capabilities.blocks: the entire mechanistic goal AND meaningful co-located validation at high elevations

requires_capabilities.capability: snow/SWE model output (H2OSNO, SWE, snow depth) with sub-monthly resolution
requires_capabilities.why: Needed to extract peak SWE and melt-out timing for comparison to SNOTEL.
Snowpack and cold-content must equilibrate before peak-SWE statistics are meaningful.

requires_capabilities.capability: DEM/elevation raster sampling for column placement
requires_capabilities.why: Needed to expand elevation bands into concrete columns and to pin columns to SNOTEL station elevations.
requires_capabilities.blocks: downstream expansion of the sampling strategy

requires_capabilities.why: Needed to compute bias/RMSE/timing metrics against the 5 stations.

requires_capabilities.capability: additional in-domain SWE observations (snow course / gridded SWE reanalysis)
requires_capabilities.why: 5 point stations cannot validate mid-band and alpine SWE across the gradient.
requires_capabilities.blocks: validation of the gradient away from station elevations

assumptions: The 5 SNOTEL stations lie within the HUC 17020011 bbox and span a useful subset of the elevation range.
Baseline forcing years (1980-2018) overlap the SNOTEL observation record for co-located comparison.
Soil/surface heterogeneity has second-order influence on peak SWE relative to forcing; elevation is treated as the primary axis.
Until downscaled forcing exists, exploratory columns test snow physics under uniform forcing, NOT the true elevation-SWE relationship.
open_questions: Is any elevation-downscaling (lapse-rate) forcing product available, or must all columns share one gridded forcing?
What are the exact SNOTEL station elevations and their period of record?
Should validation weight peak-SWE magnitude or melt-out timing more heavily for the intended application?
